text:
maria_support: Heads-up: customer acme reports immediate SSO breaks after their IdP rotated keys ~2h ago. They see a 403 on our ACS endpoint, only for the new key. Old log snippet shows assertion signed with key id 'k-ecdsa-02' and new one 'k-ecdsa-03'.
kevin_engineering: can you paste the exact error from our side?
maria_support: pasted below — short repro from curl hitting our /sso/acs endpoint: 
```
curl -v -X POST 'https://our-app.example.com/sso/acs/tenant/acme' -H 'Content-Type: application/xml' --data-binary @saml-response.xml
> POST /sso/acs/tenant/acme HTTP/2
< HTTP/2 403
< x-request-id: zyx-12345
< content-type: text/plain; charset=utf-8
< content-encoding: br

403: SAML signature verification failed: no matching IdP signing key found (kid=k-ecdsa-03)
```
kevin_engineering: thanks. I pulled our metadata fetch logs — we fetched the IdP metadata at 2026-03-18T10:02:01Z and got a 200 with ETag: W/"v45" (weak ETag). The IdP rotated and reissued metadata at 10:05, but their server responded 304 to our poll due to caching heuristics; watcher ignored body because of the weak ETag handling.
sam_sre: timeline looks like: metadata watcher fetched at 10:02 -> parsed ACS list (two entries, both index=0), our ACS selection prefers the first Binding="urn:oasis:names:..." entry. IdP's new metadata reordered entries and removed isDefault attribute on the new ACS. Our parser then cached the wrong ACS->assertion recipient mismatch in some cases (we're tolerant usually, but when signature uses the new key and recipient doesn't match EXACT URL we return 403).
maria_support: customer also sent their IdP metadata snippet (redacted):
```
<EntityDescriptor entityID="https://login.acme-idp.com">
  <IDPSSODescriptor>
    <KeyDescriptor use="signing">
      <KeyInfo>...k-ecdsa-03 public key...</KeyInfo>
    </KeyDescriptor>
    <AssertionConsumerService index="0" Binding="urn:oasis:names:...:HTTP-POST" Location="https://our-app.example.com/sso/acs/tenant/acme/"/>
    <AssertionConsumerService index="0" Binding="urn:oasis:names:...:HTTP-POST" Location="https://our-app.example.com/sso/acs/tenant/acme"/>
  </IDPSSODescriptor>
</EntityDescriptor>
```
kevin_engineering: ah — two ACS entries with identical index and same Binding, differing only by trailing slash. Our recipient canonicalization code normalizes trailing slashes in runtime checks, but the signature's Recipient in the Assertion was without slash, and our ACS selection picked the slash variant. Because the Recipient string inside the signed assertion didn't match the ACS Location we validated against, verification failed even though logically they point to same URL.
maria_support: customer says they haven't changed the ACS they send in assertions; IdP changed metadata and key.
ida_idp-bot: metadata-checker alert: fetched metadata 10:05:02Z, content-encoding: br, content-type: text/plain (non-xml); parser accepted after brotli decode but logged a warning about content-type mismatch.
sam_sre: couple of action items I see: 1) short-term workaround: add tolerant recipient matching (allow trailing slash normalization when checking Recipient vs ACS Location) behind a feature flag for support tenants; 2) refresh metadata immediately for acme (force poll and clear watcher cache); 3) improve ETag handling to treat weak ETags as possible updates when body differs (or rely on Last-Modified if present).
kevin_engineering: agree. Also: add explicit check to match key ids (kid) against KeyDescriptor value and fall back to alternate keys in metadata. Our current key lookup assumes unique key ids and fails when IdP rotates and reorders keys quickly.
maria_support: I've asked the customer for their SAMLResponse (base64) and one matching raw assertion with Recipient value. They sent it and Recipient is "https://our-app.example.com/sso/acs/tenant/acme" (no trailing slash).
jane_acme: thanks for the quick responses. We rotated keys in the IdP because of a scheduled rollover, but didn't intend to change ACS ordering. We'll keep metadata TTL short going forward. Is there anything we should change on our side?
sam_sre: for now no changes from your side. We'll do a forced metadata refresh and enable trailing-slash tolerant matching for acme only. ETA ~ 45m.
kevin_engineering: dev-note for patch: update recipient-match logic to first exact-match against normalized URL (strip trailing slash) and if signature verification fails, retry checking other ACS entries with normalized compare. Also make metadata watcher treat weak ETag as "maybe stale" and fetch body if Last-Modified differs. I'll open PR and link here.
kevin_engineering: PR #4028 created: "sso: tolerant recipient matching + metadata weak-etag fix" — cc @sam_sre for deploy scheduling.
maria_support: I've sent customer instructions to retry after we flip the feature flag; asked them to hold off rotating again until we confirm. They appreciated the temporary workaround. :thumbsup:
sam_sre: scheduling deploy to staging in 10m, smoke tests include: 1) matching assertion with/without trailing slash; 2) metadata rotation with weak ETag->304->body-change scenario; 3) key-id reorder quick-rotate test.
ida_idp-bot: deploy pipeline: staging job queued by sam_sre at 10:40Z.
kevin_engineering: I'll monitor logs for zyx-12345 request id and report back.
maria_support: marking this thread escalated -> eng. Updating support ticket with timeline and our mitigation steps.
kevin_engineering: update: staging ran, tests passed, enabling flag for tenant acme in prod routing table now.
sam_sre: prod flip done 11:20Z, customer retried and confirmed SSO succeeded. jane_acme: confirmed login works now, thanks team!
maria_support: closing the immediate escalation. Will follow up with a postmortem on the watcher ETag semantics and add docs for customers: "IdP metadata best practices: unique ACS indexes, avoid duplicate indexes, avoid weak ETag caching or ensure Last-Modified updates."
